From exploration to research figures

The five selected findings cover price skew, the horsepower–price relationship, differences by vehicle size, uneven model-year patterns, and missing-data limitations. The fifth finding uses two figures so field-level missingness and fuel-group selection remain clear.

Each original image is preserved from Assignment 5. Redesigns use the same cleaned data, with analysis-specific subsets stated below each figure. Chart types are changed when they improve communication and retained when they already fit the question. All figures are static, with embedded images and text summaries for accessibility.

FIGURE 1 · ASSIGNMENT 5 CHART 1

Recorded prices have a long upper tail

Mean MSRP is $41,926, above the $30,675 median. The price distribution is right-skewed.

Design decisions

Chart type
Retain a histogram to show the full distribution, combining the original two panels into one.
Title
State the takeaway instead of naming only the variable.
Labels
Show readable dollar amounts instead of scientific notation or log10 values.
Scale
Use a labeled logarithmic x-axis; the count axis begins at zero.
Legend
Identify median and mean with values and distinct line styles.
Annotation
Mark the median and mean directly on the distribution.
Layout
Use one large plot with room for tick labels.
Visual hierarchy
Green bars establish the distribution; solid and dashed lines emphasize summaries.
Accessibility
High-contrast colors, solid/dashed lines, descriptive alternative text, and a text finding.

Research connection: Use robust price summaries in the paper and explain why log-price analysis is useful.

PNG figure · Scalable SVG figure

FIGURE 2 · ASSIGNMENT 5 CHART 4

Horsepower is positively associated with price

Across 11,130 complete pairs, Pearson r is 0.659 for horsepower and MSRP, and 0.685 for horsepower and log10(MSRP).

Design decisions

Chart type
Replace overlapping scatter points with a density hexbin plot.
Title
Describe the observed relationship without a causal claim.
Labels
Name horsepower, currency, and the logarithmic price axis.
Scale
Retain log price; use a labeled log color scale for bin counts.
Legend
Provide a numeric density colorbar.
Annotation
Display sample size and both clearly distinguished correlations.
Layout
Separate the density legend from the main plotting area.
Visual hierarchy
Dense regions lead the eye; a compact note gives supporting statistics.
Accessibility
Sequential light-to-dark shading, text statistics, axis units, and alternative text.

Research connection: Use this as evidence of association and consider brand, size, and model year as potential confounders.

PNG figure · Scalable SVG figure

FIGURE 3 · ASSIGNMENT 5 CHART 3

Vehicle size separates median prices

Median MSRP increases from $23,650 for compact to $33,295 for midsize and $39,970 for large vehicles.

Design decisions

Chart type
Use a median-and-IQR interval plot for a focused group comparison.
Title
Emphasize the ordering of group medians.
Labels
Show group sample sizes and exact median prices.
Scale
Use a linear dollar axis beginning at zero for easy distance comparisons.
Legend
Explain interval and dot meanings inside the chart.
Annotation
Directly label every median.
Layout
Horizontal categories allow readable group names.
Visual hierarchy
High-contrast median dots stand out from the supporting IQR intervals.
Accessibility
Position and text convey differences without relying on color.

Research connection: Compare typical prices while acknowledging overlapping IQRs; the original box plot retains full-distribution context.

PNG figure · Scalable SVG figure

FIGURE 4 · ASSIGNMENT 5 CHART 6

Model-year coverage limits trend interpretation

Median recorded MSRP jumps from $2,561 in 2000 to $22,768 in 2001; 2015–2017 account for 51.46% of records.

Design decisions

Chart type
Replace the connected price line with unconnected dots; retain aligned count bars.
Title
Call attention to the abrupt shift.
Labels
Name model year and recorded-price units explicitly.
Scale
Use zero-based linear axes for medians and group counts.
Legend
Panel axis labels identify both measures without an extra legend.
Annotation
Label the 2000–2001 change and recent-year share.
Layout
Align the two panels on the same year axis.
Visual hierarchy
Price comparison is primary; counts provide supporting context.
Accessibility
Readable ticks, high contrast, and a textual warning against a historical-growth interpretation.

Research connection: Discuss source-price construction and uneven coverage before interpreting model-year differences.

PNG figure · Scalable SVG figure

FIGURE 5 · ASSIGNMENT 5 CHART 8

Missing data are concentrated in selected fields

Market category is missing in 3,376 records (30.15%); horsepower is missing in 69 records (0.62%).

Design decisions

Chart type
Keep horizontal bars but omit nine zero-missing fields from the plot, disclosed in the caption.
Title
State which field dominates missingness.
Labels
Replace code-style field names with readable labels; show counts and percentages.
Scale
Keep one zero-based percentage scale so the large gap remains honest.
Legend
Use direct field labels instead of a legend.
Annotation
Attach exact count and rate to every bar, including tiny bars.
Layout
Sort from most to least missing.
Visual hierarchy
Highlight market category with a blue accent and keep the rest uniform.
Accessibility
Text values remain readable when small bars are hard to see; color is not the only cue.

Research connection: Use analysis-specific subsets rather than dropping all records with any missing field.

PNG figure · Scalable SVG figure

FIGURE 6 · ASSIGNMENT 5 CHART 9

Horsepower exclusions disproportionately affect electric records

Horsepower is missing for 44 of 66 electric records (66.7%), compared with 25 of 11,130 known non-electric records (0.22%).

Design decisions

Chart type
Retain horizontal percentage bars because they support this comparison well.
Title
Make the selection issue explicit.
Labels
Show numerator, denominator, and percentage for every group.
Scale
Use a complete 0–100% scale.
Legend
Direct category labels eliminate a separate legend.
Annotation
Place missing/total labels next to bars, including the zero value.
Layout
Put the affected electric group first.
Visual hierarchy
The largest bar communicates the contrast; denominators temper interpretation.
Accessibility
Single-color bars, direct numeric labels, alternative text, and a text summary.

Research connection: Report this selection limitation alongside the horsepower–price figure. It is a descriptive association, not proof of a missing-data mechanism.

Research use, limitations, and reproducibility

Figures 1–4 are candidates for the Results section. Figures 5–6 document data quality and selection limitations in the Methods or Limitations section. These descriptive comparisons do not demonstrate causal effects or statistical significance. Vehicle specifications and trims are not a random sample of actual sales, and related records may not be independent.

The cleaned dataset contains 11,199 records after 715 exact duplicates were removed from 11,914 original rows. No additional global exclusions or imputations were made for this assignment. Recorded MSRP is not a verified current transaction price. Price-floor records and extreme prices remain included.

Source: Cooper Union, Car Features and MSRP, Kaggle. Preparation: Assignment 3. Findings and originals: Assignment 5.

Cleaned dataset · Reproduction script

Run python build_assignment6.py with pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib installed, beside data_cleaned.csv and the original eda_figures folder. PNGs are suitable for documents; SVGs scale cleanly for the research paper.
